from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines_raw = ["Wordle is about reducing uncertainty.", "Each guess eliminates impossible candidates.", "Think of a sieve for words."]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Concept: Entropy", lecture_lines_raw)
        
        # Animation Elements
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.05, color=WHITE) for _ in range(36)])
        dots.arrange_in_grid(6, 6, buff=0.1)
        # Addressed issue 21/35: Fix dot grid layout
        self.place_in_area(dots, 'B4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.5)
        
        entropy_formula = MathTex(r"H(X) = -\sum p(x) \log p(x)", color="#FFFF00")
        # Addressed issue 19/34: Fix entropy formula layout
        self.place_in_area(entropy_formula, 'A1', 'A6', scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(dots), FadeIn(entropy_formula))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(dots.animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Information theory creates computational efficiency.",
            "Minimize bits of remaining uncertainty.",
            "Collapse candidates into the target."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Reiterate the entropy concept summary
        entropy_text = Text("Entropy = Uncertainty", font_size=36, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(entropy_text, "B2", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(FadeIn(entropy_text))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display the optimal strategy flowchart
        flowchart = VGroup(
            Rectangle(height=0.5, width=1.5, color=GREY),
            Arrow(UP, DOWN, color=GREY),
            Rectangle(height=0.5, width=1.5, color=GREY)
        ).arrange(DOWN)
        self.place_in_area(flowchart, "A3", "C5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Create(flowchart))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Final takeaway: uncertainty reduction is key
        dot_cloud = VGroup(*[Dot(radius=0.03) for _ in range(50)])
        dot_cloud.arrange_in_grid(5, 10, buff=0.1)
        self.place_at_grid(dot_cloud, "E4", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(dot_cloud))
        self.play(dot_cloud.animate.scale(0.1).set_opacity(0.3))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: Mastering Wordle: Information Theory and Optimal Strategies
outline.target_audience: University students interested in Computer Science and Data Analytics

sections.title: The Core Concept: Entropy
sections.content: Introduce information entropy (Shannon Entropy) as the measure of uncertainty reduction. Explain that each guess is a tool to eliminate the maximum number of impossible candidates from the dictionary.
sections.example: Imagine a bowl of 2,300 M&Ms (the dictionary). A good guess is like a sieve that removes as many as possible, leaving only a small, manageable handful.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Probability & Visual Mapping
sections.content: Briefly define the 'State Space' of a guess (Green, Yellow, Gray). Visualize the game as a Decision Tree where every branch reduces the branching factor of the search space.
sections.example: Visualizing the search space as a Venn Diagram where the intersection of 'contains A' and 'ends in E' shrinks the potential word pool from 2,300 to 50.

sections.title: Algorithmic Strategy: The 'Best' First Guess
sections.content: Analyze why high-frequency letters (e.g., E, A, R, I, O, T) are superior. Introduce the algorithm: Minimax (minimizing the maximum remaining words) or Max Entropy.
sections.example: Comparing 'XYLYL' (low entropy) vs 'CRANE' (high entropy). Show a bar chart animation where 'CRANE' leaves a more uniform distribution of potential remaining sets.

sections.title: Tactical Application: The 'Hard Mode' Trap
sections.content: Discuss the trade-off between choosing the 'most likely' word versus the 'best information' word. Sometimes, sacrificing a guess to eliminate multiple letter options is statistically better.
sections.example: A clever 'Robot Assistant' character choosing 'SLATE' to eliminate 5 common letters, even though it knows 'SLATE' isn't the target, to guarantee the answer on turn 3.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
sections.content: Recap: Information Theory transforms Wordle from a game of intuition into a game of computational efficiency. The optimal path is always minimizing the 'bits' of remaining uncertainty.
sections.example: A quick visual animation: Starting with a giant cloud of 2,300 words, seeing it collapse into a single point after just 3 optimized moves.
